parole.significato: A humanoid or apelike animal said to exist in the Himalayas.
parole.testo: First attested in 1921. Calque of Tibetan མི་སྡུག་གངས་མི (mi sdug gangs mi), from མི་སྡུག (mi sdug, “repulsive, unlovely, ugly, hideous”) and གངས་མི (gangs mi, “snowman”).

parole.significato: The state of existence between death and subsequent reincarnation.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Tibetan བར་དོ (bar do), from བར (bar, “interval”) + དོ (do, “two”), in the sense of an interval between two states.

parole.significato: A Tibetan stupa, typically spindle-shaped and white.

parole.testo: Borrowed from Tibetan ཕྱུ་པ (phyu pa), from Arabic جُبَّة (jubba). Doublet of jupe and jubbah.

parole.significato: The second-highest-ranking lama of the Gelug sect of Tibetan Buddhism, after the Dalai Lama.
parole.testo: Tibetan པན་ཆེན་བླ་མ (pan chen bla ma). From Sanskrit पण्डित (paṇḍita, “scholar”) + Tibetan ཆེན་པོ (chen po, “big”) + Tibetan བླ་མ (bla ma).

parole.significato: A title indicating great respect, prefixed to the names of Tibetan Buddhists.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Tibetan པད་མ (pad ma), from Sanskrit पद्म (padma, “lotus”). Doublet of Padma.

parole.significato: A Tibetan Buddhist discipline supposed to create heat in the body.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Tibetan གཏུམ་མོ (gtum mo, literally “fierce woman”).
